abstract: Continuous behavioural monitoring is essential for assessing animal welfare and individual behavioural variation, yet traditional observation-based methods are labour-intensive and prone to bias. Here, we developed a modular framework with computer vision for automated behavioural profiling of group-housed Beagles, integrating You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based models for pose estimation, individual identification, and enrichment detection. A ceiling-mounted infrared camera system enabled uninterrupted monitoring under standard kennel conditions. The identity-independent YOLO-POSE model achieved 99% precision, 97% recall, and an mAP50 of 0.98, while the YOLO classification model reached 95% accuracy for individual identification without external markers. Combining posture, identity, and environmental information enabled automated quantification of spatial use, locomotor activity, social interactions, corridor-oriented behaviour, drinking behaviour, and enrichment use. Overall, this framework captured distinct behavioural profiles of individual dogs from the same litter housed in the same kennel, which can be used to assess animal welfare and to evaluate environmental enrichments objectively. Together, we demonstrate a scalable and non-invasive approach for continuous individual behavioural profiling of group-housed dogs for computational ethology and translational research. By separating pose estimation from identity assignment, the framework enables flexible deployment across changing social groups and facilitates application to previously unseen individuals with minimal training.
